originalFindings.title: Substrate Inspection Documentation Discrepancy and Resolution

originalFindings.consequence: Work progress was contingent on formal acceptance despite verbal instructions; historical discrepancy noted for retrospective audit.
originalFindings.action: Retrospective confirmation that substrate inspection QC-B104-0514 matches work records to validate closeout documentation.
originalFindings.uncertainty: No

originalFindings.title: RFI-017 Design Decision Transmission and Slab Detail Clarification

originalFindings.consequence: Lack of a formally transmitted design decision and attached record prevents audit closure and relies on internal notes rather than approved shop drawings for the replacement slab detail.
originalFindings.action: Attach formal RFI response to verify the approved slab detail and resolve the technical query before closing out the concern.
originalFindings.uncertainty: Confidence is limited by missing attachment of the formal RFI-017 response despite claims of resolution in daily reports.

Attach formal RFI response and reinforcement inspection record; maintain curing/protection; notify adjacent trades when access is safe.

originalFindings.consequence: Work schedule impacted by administrative hold; physical completion achieved after documentation gap reconciliation.
originalFindings.action: Verify delay duration impact against project baseline if required for claims history.
originalFindings.uncertainty: RFI-017 response attached status uncertain in A09 despite claim of resolution; internal note in A06 suggests decision made but formal system response missing.

ISS-01.note: Unknown water cause preserved; possible leak locations are hypotheses, not asserted causes.

ISS-02.note: Earlier undocumented acceptance and later signed QC-B104-0514 closure reconciled.

ISS-03.note: Readiness/verbal direction distinguished from written acceptance and later signed closure.

ISS-04.note: Prior open query and final resolution claim identified, but open-through-May system status is broader than supplied evidence.

ISS-05.note: Hold/completion dates identified, but says documentation gap was reconciled before completion despite remaining record gaps.

ISS-06.note: GC readiness and subcontractor missing release identified; specific GC claim that inspection passed is not explicitly compared.

ISS-07.note: Slab-detail and missing revision concern recognized, but whole finding overstates latest system status.

ISS-08.note: Transmission gap identified but latest status assertion needs correction.

ISS-09.note: Inspection reference/record gap identified, but report author is misattributed and selected A09 field does not show the inspection reference.

ISS-10.note: Reported resolution and missing formal record identified, with overbroad open-through-May assertion.

ISS-11.note: Quantity is correctly distinguished. Strength follow-up appears in F7 but its sole cited field does not support that statement.

ISS-12.note: Temporary adjacent-trade effect and uncertainty about notice correctly framed; no full-shift or critical-path claim.

findingNotes.F1: Supported chronology and signed acceptance; uncertainty No is terse but the reported closure is explicit.
findingNotes.F2: Until pour implies a transmission time not established by the reports.
findingNotes.F3: A09 is the GC superintendent report, not Concrete Subcontractor. Its selected supporting_evidence field does not contain RI-B104-0515.
findingNotes.F4: Remained open in system through May 2026 is broader than the May 11–15 record and not established by A09. Conservative whole-finding judgment; independent adjudication may assess this wording differently.
findingNotes.F5: Completion after documentation-gap reconciliation is unsupported; the gap remains in A09.
findingNotes.F6: Supported delivered-versus-measured-installed distinction.
findingNotes.F7: Correct follow-up fact, but wrong cited field: needs A09 schedule_status, not issue_or_update.
findingNotes.F8: Supported unknown cause and proposed investigation; potential leak sources are explicitly possible.
findingNotes.F9: Supported temporary restriction/uncertain notification inquiry. Duration/reassignment not elaborated, but no larger delay is asserted.

reports.work_planned: Remove water-damaged concrete flooring and prepare substrate for replacement.

reports.issue_or_update: Water damage was observed near the east wall. The source has not been confirmed. No standing water remained at the start of the shift.
reports.schedule_status: Removal is progressing; substrate inspection required before replacement pour.

reports.schedule_status: Base preparation may proceed, subject to confirmation of inspection requirements.
reports.action_required: Confirm whether the substrate inspection has occurred and record acceptance before the pour.
reports.supporting_evidence: No inspection checklist attached

reports.work_planned: Complete base preparation and place replacement concrete if area is released.
reports.work_completed: Base preparation completed over approximately 18 m2. No concrete placed.

reports.supporting_evidence: Crew foreman notes verbal instruction; no signed inspection form attached

reports.work_planned: Resolve inspection status and coordinate concrete placement.

reports.schedule_status: Report indicates inspection passed; subcontractor records indicate pour remains on hold.
reports.action_required: Reconcile inspection status with the inspector and subcontractor; circulate the signed release and confirm whether RFI-017 is answered.
reports.supporting_evidence: Call notes only; no inspection record attached

reports.work_planned: Place replacement concrete after receipt of approved release and mix details.
reports.work_completed: No concrete placed. Crew completed edge cleaning and staged reinforcement materials outside the work area.
reports.materials_equipment: Reinforcement materials staged; concrete pump not mobilized

reports.schedule_status: Pour postponed for a second shift. Crew reassigned for part of the afternoon.
reports.action_required: Issue inspection release and provide written response to RFI-017 before rescheduling the pour.
reports.responsible_party: General Contractor / Quality Inspector / Design Team
reports.supporting_evidence: Foreman log; no formal response attached

reports.work_planned: Review RFI and confirm repair scope.
reports.work_completed: RFI-017 reviewed internally. Engineer's note says 'use original detail' but the response was not transmitted through the formal RFI system.
reports.issue_or_update: Internal note may be interpreted as a decision, but there is no formally issued response or confirmation that the subcontractor received it.
reports.schedule_status: Subcontractor may remain on hold until formal response is distributed.
reports.action_required: Issue the formal RFI response, confirm receipt, and identify the applicable drawing revision.
reports.supporting_evidence: Internal engineering note; formal response not attached

reports.work_planned: Verify substrate and pre-pour readiness.
reports.work_completed: Inspection completed at 08:10. Substrate accepted for placement subject to using the approved slab detail and documenting reinforcement placement. Signed checklist recorded as QC-B104-0514.
reports.issue_or_update: The signed checklist confirms substrate acceptance, but does not resolve the slab thickness question in RFI-017.
reports.schedule_status: Substrate inspection closed; pour still depends on design clarification and reinforcement verification.
reports.action_required: Design Team to issue formal slab detail; subcontractor to request reinforcement inspection before placement.
reports.supporting_evidence: Signed checklist QC-B104-0514 referenced

reports.work_planned: Place replacement concrete after design and inspection release.
reports.work_completed: Reinforcement placed over the prepared area. No concrete placed.

reports.schedule_status: Pour not started. Reinforcement inspection requested but not yet completed.
reports.action_required: Confirm approved drawing revision and complete reinforcement inspection before placement.
reports.responsible_party: General Contractor / Design Team / Quality Inspector
reports.supporting_evidence: Message referenced but not attached; no reinforcement inspection record

reports.work_planned: Coordinate concrete placement and adjacent trade access.

reports.issue_or_update: Report states the pour used the approved detail, but does not cite the drawing revision or attach the formal RFI-017 response. Reinforcement inspection reference is listed as RI-B104-0515.
reports.schedule_status: Placement completed; curing/protection and strength-test follow-up remain in progress.

reports.supporting_evidence: Delivery tickets referenced; RFI response not attached

reports.schedule_status: No full-shift delay reported; local work sequence changed.
reports.rfi_change_order_refs: No RFI or change order referenced
reports.action_required: GC to confirm access notification procedure for adjacent trades and record any verified schedule impact.

ISS-01.note: Quotes the observed water damage and unconfirmed source with needs_verification and no invented cause.

ISS-02.note: Preserves the initial missing formal acceptance/release and closes substrate acceptance using explicit acceptance and signed checklist QC-B104-0514.

ISS-03.note: Preserves apparent readiness without inspection sign-off and missing workface release, followed by signed substrate acceptance. It does not treat apparent readiness as proof of acceptance.

ISS-04.note: Together the supported technical and communication findings preserve the earlier unanswered question, internal/informal direction, later reported RFI resolution, and missing formal response/revision. They do not assert that the technical decision is proven unresolved.

ISS-05.note: Quotes actual pour postponement across earlier dates, partial-afternoon crew reassignment, the subsequent hold and later completed placement. Historical state correctly ends the work-progress concern without implying record gaps or prerequisites were independently verified closed.

ISS-06.note: Preserves the GC inspection-passed account versus the missing written release and reconciles substrate acceptance through the later signed checklist.

ISS-07.note: Preserves original thickness versus revised detail, internal and informal instruction, missing drawing/revision, and the latest approved-detail claim without its linked formal response.

ISS-08.note: Preserves the internal response not formally transmitted, unconfirmed receipt, missing revision and latest missing formal response evidence.

ISS-09.note: F6 preserves the earlier requested-but-not-completed reinforcement inspection and later bare inspection reference with needs_verification. F11 separately preserves the explicit open task to attach the inspection record. No supported finding is used to establish that the bare reference proves inspection acceptance.

ISS-10.note: Preserves the superintendent resolved label and explicit outstanding formal-response attachment task/missing-response evidence, with open record-task state.

ISS-11.note: Delivered versus separately unmeasured placed volume is correctly captured. F10/F11 include the instruction to maintain curing/protection, but no output quotes the explicitly unfinished strength-test follow-up, so this combined quantity/quality closeout reference remains partial.

ISS-12.note: F8 preserves reported notice versus uncertainty about foreman advance notice. F16 separately preserves the ended 09:00-12:45 restriction, reassignment/resumption, three-hour-45-minute duration and no-full-shift statement. No critical-path impact is inferred.

findingNotes.F1: Correct unconfirmed cause, no invented source of water damage.
findingNotes.F2: Correct substrate acceptance and earlier readiness/passed-versus-missing-release evidence. Explicit conditional acceptance and signed checklist support substrate-only closure.
findingNotes.F3: Duplicate of F2 for the same missing written substrate release and signed checklist closure; all selected evidence is a subset of F2.
findingNotes.F4: Correct original-versus-revised slab question, informal/internal direction and latest missing formal response/revision. Needs_verification describes evidence limitations rather than proof that no technical answer existed.
findingNotes.F5: Correct uncertain formal transmission/receipt, including reported RFI resolution and missing formal response. This is a communication-verification aspect, not a claim that work is still physically on hold.
findingNotes.F6: Correct reinforcement inspection acceptance uncertainty: earlier incomplete inspection plus later bare reference, with no closure asserted.
findingNotes.F7: Correct delivered-versus-unmeasured placed quantity; no fabricated placed volume, wastage or invalid unit comparison.
findingNotes.F8: Correct uncertain notice/receipt coordination aspect. It does not assert that the GC gave no notice or that the restriction lasted a full shift.
findingNotes.F9: Correct historical actual pour postponement and later completed placement, with no claim that document gaps were therefore closed.
findingNotes.F10: Supported distinct open task to attach the formal RFI response. This concrete record-submission requirement differs from F5 uncertainty about whether a formal response was issued/received, although sources overlap.
findingNotes.F11: Supported distinct open task to attach the reinforcement inspection record. It does not claim inspection acceptance; F6 separately keeps that physical acceptance uncertain.
findingNotes.F12: Duplicate of F4 for the same slab-detail/drawing-revision uncertainty and latest missing formal record. Additional source context does not introduce another distinct concern.
findingNotes.F13: Duplicate of the resolved substrate-release aspect already in F2, with overlapping historical delay context in F9. Resolved is interpreted narrowly as the written substrate gate, which the selected signed checklist supports. The same finding explicitly quotes other still-pending design/reinforcement gates; it is not accepted as proof that the whole pour was already completed on May 14.
findingNotes.F14: Duplicate of F4/F5 for the same earlier technical-question/formal-response gap, with historical delay context already in F9. Needs_verification is read as the formal RFI evidence aspect, not an assertion that concrete placement remained postponed after completion.
findingNotes.F15: Duplicate of F9 for an ended work-progress hold: it explicitly quotes Concrete placement completed. Resolved is accepted only for that physical progress aspect, not as inspection acceptance inferred from RI-B104-0515. F6 and F11 retain the separate acceptance/record uncertainty. The latest-pointer placement on the bare reference should not be treated as proof of passed inspection.
findingNotes.F16: Supported distinct historical trade disruption with reassignment/resumption and bounded duration. Its physical work-sequence state ended; F8 separately retains uncertainty about notification.
findingNotes.F17: Duplicate of F2 for the same verbal/passed-versus-written substrate release concern and later signed closure, with additional historical detail but no new outstanding aspect.
findingNotes.F18: Duplicate of F5 for the same formal RFI transmission/receipt evidence gap and latest reported resolution without attached response.

evaluation.notes: Actual uploaded-sample UI run, original datasetId custom preserved; evaluationDatasetId reports-a is a scoring alias justified by the exact normalized input hash. Provisional score: 11/12 fully found, one partial, no unsupported findings and seven duplicates across 18 original outputs. Eleven distinct outputs are supported under the duplicate-excluding precision rule. F13/F15 states are accepted narrowly for substrate-gate or physical-progress closure, never as unsupported proof of reinforcement acceptance; these scopes are explicitly noted because the generic progress heading can be ambiguous. F10/F11 open attachment tasks remain distinct from uncertain formal transmission or physical acceptance. Strength-test follow-up is omitted. A informed development. A separate Codex agent is not an independent human adjudicator.

F-01.note: Fully retains verbal isolation-proved accounts versus unavailable signed crew certificate, then explicit signed issue/receipt and closed written branch-isolation acceptance. Does not conflate this with replacement pressure-test acceptance.

F-02.note: Retains the 0-10 V versus 4-20 mA conflict, unapproved internal draft, and later signed TQ-074 / E-620 revision H decision specifying 4-20 mA. Correct resolved technical-choice status.

F-03.note: Captures the earlier unapproved/unregistered draft and lack of an issued crew instruction, followed by formal signed issue and supersession. No selected finding retains the explicit August 20 10:25 acknowledgement by both installation supervisors. Formal issue alone does not fully cover the separately defined receipt-confirmation concern, so this reference remains partial.

F-04.note: F7 retains the August 19 08:00-11:20 hold, reassignment, 3-hour-20-minute duration and August 21 physical fitting completion. F11 retains the missing release/interface prerequisites and subsequent gate closures. Together they cover the whole historical event once, without full-shift, commissioning-completion or critical-path claims.

F-05.note: Captures requested pressure-test witness, later PT-V24-0822 register entry, unavailable/unlinked signed acceptance sheet, and record verification before insulation closeout. The open label applies to the explicit record-linking/verification task; it does not assert a failed or never-performed pressure test. Branch-isolation acceptance is correctly closed separately in F1.

F-06.note: Correctly retains the measured 360 L recovered versus 300 L transfer record, unreconciled 60 L and open collection/tank-balance reconciliation. No invented spill, disposal breach or cause.

F-07.note: Explicitly distinguishes completed local stroke exercise from unperformed remote command, feedback and fail-safe tests, and retains the remaining acceptance before automatic service. No invented failed or overdue test.

F-08.note: Jointly captures the 70-minute ceiling restriction, two installers reassigned and later resumed access, alongside reportedly sent advance email and unestablished crew receipt. Historical disruption and outstanding receipt follow-up are kept distinct and the reference is counted once.

findingNotes.F1: Supported full verbal-versus-written isolation-release concern with explicit signed later closure and receipt. Most complete primary item for F-01.
findingNotes.F2: Duplicate of F14: same conflicting control-signal detail, unapproved draft and later signed technical decision. F14 additionally retains the historical absence of an issued installer instruction, so it is retained as the more complete technical/communication item.
findingNotes.F3: Supported pressure-test record verification gap. Open is interpreted as the known remaining record-linking task rather than a claim that the test failed or never occurred; selected passages expressly limit the uncertainty to verification of acceptance.
findingNotes.F4: Supported measured-fluid versus signed-transfer quantity discrepancy, retaining both source measurements, amount and open reconciliation.
findingNotes.F5: Supported outstanding remote functional acceptance despite completed local exercise, with explicit service condition and no overdue/failure claim.
findingNotes.F6: Duplicate/subset of F16: same reportedly sent access email and unknown receipt. F16 retains that concern plus the now-restored access context; no distinct communication issue is added here.
findingNotes.F7: Supported historical measured work-area hold, reassignment and later physical fitting completion. Complements F11 prerequisite/gate context; does not claim completion of automatic-service acceptance.
findingNotes.F8: Duplicate/subset of F3: same unlinked/unavailable pressure-test acceptance sheet and remaining verification task, with no distinct new concern.
findingNotes.F9: Duplicate of F4: same 360 L versus 300 L transfer discrepancy and unreconciled 60 L; the combined source action adds no separate quantity issue.
findingNotes.F10: Duplicate/subset of F5: same outstanding remote tests and automatic-service condition. F5 additionally preserves the actual completed local exercise.
findingNotes.F11: Supported historical prerequisite-gate hold and its later written-release/design-information closures. This complements F7 actual duration/reassignment/physical completion; resolved is confined to those stated prerequisites and is not treated as proof that fitting completed on August 20.
findingNotes.F12: Supported historical trade restriction, two-person reassignment, 70-minute duration and resumed corridor access. Its selected reported email/unknown receipt context complements the separately open follow-up in F16.
findingNotes.F13: Duplicate of F1: same verbal isolation-proved versus unavailable signed certificate and same later signed issue/receipt/closure. The added deferred-window sentence is already retained in F7/F11 and does not create an additional release concern.
findingNotes.F14: Supported technical conflict and historical unapproved/unissued instruction gap, with explicit formal revision issue and technical closure. It does not retain the actual trade receipt acknowledgements, so communication-reference F-03 is partial despite technical-reference F-02 being fully found.
findingNotes.F15: Duplicate combination of F3 and F4: repeats the pressure-test record-verification gap and fluid quantity discrepancy using the same latest passages. Both are true and remain open, but combining them adds no unique concern and is not extra precision or recall credit.
findingNotes.F16: Supported reported email sending versus uncertain receipt with historical restriction and resumed-access context. Complements F12 historical disruption; F6 is excluded as the repeated subset.

findingNotes.F1: Unsupported material review alert: the passages describe ordinary planned/completed corridor cleaning and supervisor acceptance. There is no recorded failed, missing, conflicting, delayed or formerly problematic acceptance to resolve. The quotations are accurate but routine acceptance is overincluded as a concern.
findingNotes.F2: Unsupported open quantity-reconciliation/conflict alert: all three reports state the same 60 m2 work area. No discrepancy or unfulfilled measurement/reconciliation requirement is present. Exact quote matching does not support the selected open/conflict interpretation.
findingNotes.F3: Unsupported delay/progress alert: every selected passage explicitly states on schedule with no outstanding follow-up. No historical postponement or work-sequence concern is documented. A resolved label does not make an invented prior concern valid.
findingNotes.F4: Unsupported record/communication alert: the reports explicitly reference the signed daily acceptance checklist and state that no additional record is required. There is no missing evidence, unresolved linkage or historical documentation problem. This is a routine completed record, not a material review concern.

evaluation.notes: Routine C negative control contains zero reference concerns. Browser 4B single-pass output produces four distinct unsupported review alerts, not four duplicate mentions of one alert. All passages are verbatim source text; the failure is semantic relevance and, in F2, unsupported open/conflict status. Do not describe citation validity as accuracy. Native 27B v17 returned zero findings on C/E in separately recorded runs. This provisional agent review is not independent human validation.

ISS-11.note: F6 preserves delivered-versus-unmeasured placed volume. No output retains explicitly unfinished strength-test follow-up. Partial counts as missed; this concern was already partial in the saved revision-17 candidate source.

findingNotes.F5: Supported separate reinforcement-acceptance uncertainty; bare inspection reference does not establish passed acceptance.

findingNotes.F8: Supported consolidated historical physical pour hold and later placement completion. The scope question and latest pointer constrain resolved to physical work, while separate acceptance/record findings remain open or uncertain.
findingNotes.F9: Supported explicit open formal-RFI-response attachment task, distinct from formal issue/receipt uncertainty.

ISS-01.note: Quotes the observed water damage and unconfirmed source with needs_verification and no invented cause.

ISS-02.note: Preserves the initial missing formal acceptance/release and closes substrate acceptance using explicit acceptance and signed checklist QC-B104-0514.

ISS-03.note: Preserves apparent readiness without inspection sign-off and missing workface release, followed by signed substrate acceptance. It does not treat apparent readiness as proof of acceptance.

ISS-04.note: Together the supported technical and communication findings preserve the earlier unanswered question, internal/informal direction, later reported RFI resolution, and missing formal response/revision. They do not assert that the technical decision is proven unresolved.

ISS-05.note: Supported F3 explicitly retains the May13 actual second-shift postponement; F11 retains May14 no-placement/incomplete-inspection context and May15 physical completion. Together these cover actual delay and later completion. Additional first postponement remains in redundant F8; duplicated cards are not counted as extra reference credit. The chronology is fragmented and fails H5.

ISS-06.note: Preserves the GC inspection-passed account versus the missing written release and reconciles substrate acceptance through the later signed checklist.

ISS-07.note: Preserves original thickness versus revised detail, internal and informal instruction, missing drawing/revision, and the latest approved-detail claim without its linked formal response.

ISS-08.note: Preserves the internal response not formally transmitted, unconfirmed receipt, missing revision and latest missing formal response evidence.

ISS-09.note: F5 asks whether reinforcement inspection is completed and formally recorded, retaining earlier incomplete inspection and a later bare reference with needs_verification. No passed inspection is claimed. The independent reinforcement-record attachment task is visible only inside RFI-scoped F9 and is flagged as an overmerge/scope defect.

ISS-10.note: F4 retains reported resolved RFI status versus missing formal response; F9 retains absent formal attachments and the explicit remaining attachment action. No completed formal response is inferred.

ISS-11.note: F6 retains delivered versus separately unmeasured placed volume. F10 explicitly selects the latest statement that curing/protection and strength-test follow-up remain in progress, with open quality-follow-up state. No test failure, overdue status or completion is inferred.

ISS-12.note: F7 retains reported notification versus uncertain advance foreman receipt; F12 retains bounded temporary restriction and reassignment/resumption, with no-full-shift statement. Count once.

findingNotes.F1: Supported unconfirmed water-damage cause.
findingNotes.F2: Supported substrate-only acceptance chronology, opposing verbal/passed versus missing-written-release accounts, and signed closure.
findingNotes.F3: Supported technical slab-detail/revision uncertainty, reported RFI resolution without linked revision/response, and actual earlier postponement context.
findingNotes.F4: Supported formal RFI-response issue/crew-receipt uncertainty.
findingNotes.F5: Supported reinforcement inspection/record acceptance uncertainty; the bare later reference is not treated as a passed inspection.
findingNotes.F6: Supported delivered versus unmeasured placed quantity.
findingNotes.F7: Supported reported notice versus unestablished advance foreman receipt.
findingNotes.F8: Semantic duplicate: prerequisite-specific work-hold fragment repeats F2 substrate-gate closure and the same actual pour chronology split across F3/F11. Its resolved label is accepted narrowly for the signed substrate prerequisite, not physical pour completion or other approvals. This is an H5 failure, not an additional useful alert.
findingNotes.F9: Supported for its RFI-record question, but independently needed reinforcement-record submission was merged into this RFI-only scope. Exact source action contains both record tasks; the question does not preserve the second aspect. Recorded separately as an overmerge/scope failure rather than inventing a false factual assertion.
findingNotes.F10: Supported explicit remaining curing/protection and strength-test follow-up, open. The actual strength requirement is verbatim in the displayed latest source passage.
findingNotes.F11: Supported narrow physical work-hold/placement chronology, with no claim that the bare reinforcement reference proves passed acceptance.
findingNotes.F12: Supported bounded ended electrical restriction and reassignment/resumption.

ISS-01.note: Quotes the observed water damage and unconfirmed source with needs_verification and no invented cause.

ISS-02.note: Preserves the initial missing formal acceptance/release and closes substrate acceptance using explicit acceptance and signed checklist QC-B104-0514.

ISS-03.note: Preserves apparent readiness without inspection sign-off and missing workface release, followed by signed substrate acceptance. It does not treat apparent readiness as proof of acceptance.

ISS-04.note: Together the supported technical and communication findings preserve the earlier unanswered question, internal/informal direction, later reported RFI resolution, and missing formal response/revision. They do not assert that the technical decision is proven unresolved.

ISS-05.note: F8 now contains the actual dated postponements, release/design/reinforcement prerequisites and later physical placement completion in ONE complete work-progress chronology. Resolved is limited to physical placement, not independent acceptance, record or testing requirements.

ISS-06.note: Preserves the GC inspection-passed account versus the missing written release and reconciles substrate acceptance through the later signed checklist.

ISS-07.note: Preserves original thickness versus revised detail, internal and informal instruction, missing drawing/revision, and the latest approved-detail claim without its linked formal response.

ISS-08.note: Preserves the internal response not formally transmitted, unconfirmed receipt, missing revision and latest missing formal response evidence.

ISS-09.note: F5 retains earlier requested/incomplete inspection and later bare RI reference with needs_verification. F10 separately retains the explicit attachment requirement. F5 wording emphasizes a formal pre-placement completion record and can be read awkwardly; scored as an interrogative verification gap, not an assertion that inspection passed or occurred. A signed acceptance could exist yet remain unlinked, so the two questions are independently answerable.

ISS-10.note: F4 retains reported RFI resolution versus unverified formal issue/receipt; F9 independently retains the formal-response attachment gap. No completed formal response is inferred.

ISS-11.note: F6 retains delivered versus unmeasured placed quantity. F11 explicitly selects the latest source stating curing/protection and strength-test follow-up remain in progress, with open quality-follow-up state. Source-only reconsideration restored this task after an incorrect initial routine verdict; full trace retained.

ISS-12.note: F7 retains reported notice versus unestablished advance foreman receipt. F12 retains bounded historical restriction and reassignment/resumption. Count once; no full-shift or critical-path claim.

findingNotes.F1: Supported unconfirmed cause, no invented source.
findingNotes.F2: Supported substrate-only acceptance/release chronology and signed closure; written-record discrepancy is consolidated into that acceptance gate.
findingNotes.F3: Supported approved slab-detail/revision uncertainty; does not prove technical non-resolution after reported RFI closure.
findingNotes.F4: Supported separate formal-response issue/crew-receipt uncertainty.
findingNotes.F5: Supported physical inspection/acceptance verification gap under interrogative reading. The question could more clearly ask whether inspection/acceptance occurred; its completed-before-placement modifier is a wording limitation, not accepted proof of completion. Visible earlier incomplete-inspection and later bare-reference quotations plus needs_verification preserve uncertainty.
findingNotes.F6: Supported delivered-versus-unmeasured placed quantity, no invented actual volume or waste.
findingNotes.F7: Supported advance-notice receipt uncertainty, independent of restored access.
findingNotes.F8: Supported complete physical pour-hold chronology through completion. All prerequisite-specific fragments now consolidated; no separate residual hold card.
findingNotes.F9: Supported formal-RFI-response document attachment/availability gap, independent of technical issue/receipt and the separately required reinforcement record.
findingNotes.F10: Supported reinforcement-record attachment/availability requirement, independent of whether physical acceptance can be established. No RFI-only scope hides this task.
findingNotes.F11: Supported explicit remaining curing/protection and strength-test follow-up, open; no failed, overdue or completed test inferred.
findingNotes.F12: Supported ended bounded electrical-trade restriction and reassignment/resumption, independent of notice receipt.

sourceInventory.quote: Set canopy column B-17 after signed bearing-surface acceptance and the issued base layout are available.
Column remained on the lifting frame.
Crew held at B-17 from 08:00 to 10:00, then reassigned to bolt the handrail in the adjacent bay.
The site coordinator verbally advised at 08:10 that the bearing inspection had passed.
The installer had no signed bearing release at 10:00.
The issued anchor-layout revision was also awaited.
The September 1 column-setting window was deferred.
The recorded hold was two hours; no project completion-date effect has been assessed.
Bearing release BR-B17 requested; layout instruction LI-017
Provide the signed bearing release and issued layout before setting B-17.
One column remained unset.
Installer daily log records the 08:00-10:00 hold and reassignment.
Close the written bearing release and issue the approved anchor layout.
Signed bearing release BR-B17-0902 issued at 09:00 and acknowledged by the steel foreperson at 09:15.
Approved anchor layout S-117 revision 7 issued through the document register at 11:00.
BR-B17-0902 explicitly accepts the bearing surface for B-17; it does not cover the later anchor-torque witness.
Revision 7 replaces revision 6.
The register confirms the layout issue to the site coordinator, but no steel-crew receipt acknowledgement is linked.
The bearing-acceptance gate is closed.
Column setting is planned for September 3; physical setting is not reported complete today.
BR-B17-0902; LI-017; S-117 revision 7; transmittal TR-119
Obtain and link the steel foreperson's receipt acknowledgement for S-117 revision 7.
One accepted bearing surface.
Signed bearing release and foreperson acknowledgement filed.
TR-119 records formal layout issue; crew receipt remains unverified.
Set and grout B-17 using S-117 revision 7.
Column B-17 set, aligned and base grouted.
Physical setting and grouting are complete.
Anchor bolts torqued with the calibrated wrench.
The engineer attended the anchor-torque witness.
The daily log cites TW-B17-0903, but the signed witness acceptance sheet is not available in the shared folder.
No test failure is reported.
Physical setting is complete following the earlier two-hour hold.
Automatic acceptance of the separate torque record is not claimed.
S-117 revision 7; TW-B17-0903
Locate the signed torque-witness acceptance sheet and verify its result before closeout.
Six anchor bolts torqued.
Lifting log records completed setting.
Grout placement log filed.
TW-B17-0903 is a reference only; its signed result sheet is unavailable.
Check the closeout folder and continue grout protection.
Delivery count and material certificates checked and accepted.
Column remains protected; no further installation work is outstanding.
BR-B17-0902 remains signed and acknowledged.
The signed TW-B17-0903 result sheet is still unavailable, so anchor-torque acceptance cannot be verified from the register reference alone.
TR-119 remains formally issued, but the steel-crew receipt acknowledgement has not been located.
Grout strength testing is scheduled for September 5 at 10:00 and has not yet occurred.
The planned test is not overdue.
BR-B17-0902; TW-B17-0903; TR-119; grout sample GS-B17
Maintain grout protection until the required strength result is documented.
Obtain the torque-witness result sheet and the steel-crew layout receipt acknowledgement.
Three grout cubes retained for the scheduled test.
Delivery and material checks accepted.
No grout-strength result is available before the scheduled test.

G-01.note: Retains the verbal passed-bearing account versus absent signed release, then dated signed issue and foreperson acknowledgement; resolved applies to bearing release only.

G-02.note: Explicitly retains unavailable signed torque-witness result and the latest source statement that separate anchor-torque acceptance cannot be verified from the register ID alone. No failed or never-performed test is inferred; bearing release is independently closed in F1. The attended-witness detail is not quoted, a contextual omission, but the material acceptance/record distinction and latest uncertainty are preserved.

G-03.note: Retains September 1 08:00-10:00 hold, handrail reassignment, missing release/layout context, two-hour duration and September 3 physical setting/grouting completion in one chronology. Resolved is physical completion only; no project completion-date effect is inferred.

G-04.note: Explicitly retains scheduled September 5 10:00 strength testing, not-yet-performed status and absent result without claiming overdue/failure. It omits the source requirement to maintain grout protection until the strength result is documented (S050); no other finding quotes that task. The unchanged compound reference requires both testing and protection. Partial counts as missed; no half credit.

G-05.note: Retains formally issued layout/TR-119 versus missing linked steel-crew receipt acknowledgement and the still-open acknowledgement task after physical installation. It does not claim no formal instruction was issued.

findingNotes.F1: Supported complete bearing-release discrepancy and explicit signed closure.
findingNotes.F2: Supported formal layout issue versus unverified crew acknowledgement, still open.
findingNotes.F3: Supported torque-acceptance result-sheet availability/verification gap; no false pass, failure or never-performed assertion.
findingNotes.F4: Supported complete historical setting hold through later physical completion, distinct from open closeout/testing/receipt.
findingNotes.F5: Supported scheduled but unperformed strength testing, open and not overdue. The separately required protection task is missing, so the combined G-04 reference remains partial.

coverageOmissions.quote: Maintain grout protection until the required strength result is documented.
coverageOmissions.note: Never selected into the output; evidence-union preservation cannot recover an unselected task.

evaluation.notes: First completed fresh selected 18f G run after the recorded freeze, using actual UI upload and original downloads. Five findings, four of five references fully found, one partial, zero unsupported distinct findings and zero semantic duplicates. The predeclared 5/5 G coverage target FAILS because the protection-until-strength task is omitted. Source/reference definitions unchanged. All eleven selected candidates map once and all selected quotations survive; this mechanical success does not cure the semantic coverage miss. Continuous processing 541.834 seconds, n=1; model load is separate and excludes prior installation/download. Author inherited project context and also performed this provisional review; neither reference withholding nor this score is independent human validation. Earlier G18c cancellation produced no completed prediction.

score.partial_policy: Partial findings count as missed. Precision uses unique supported/unsupported output findings; recall uses reference issues.

reports.weather: Light rain outside; interior work area dry at start
reports.work_planned: Remove water-damaged concrete flooring and prepare substrate for replacement.
reports.work_completed: Removed approximately 18 m2 of flooring in Room B104. Debris placed in designated container. Exposed substrate photographed.

reports.issue_or_update: Water damage was observed near the east wall. The source has not been confirmed. No standing water remained at the start of the shift.
reports.schedule_status: Removal is progressing; substrate inspection required before replacement pour.
reports.rfi_change_order_refs: CO-01 referenced; no RFI number listed
reports.action_required: GC to confirm removal boundary and arrange substrate inspection before pour preparation.
reports.supporting_evidence: Photos B104-0511-01 to B104-0511-04 listed; not attached in this synthetic record

reports.work_planned: Coordinate repair scope and confirm area ready for replacement concrete.
reports.work_completed: Daily coordination walk completed. Superintendent noted that the flooring removal area appeared ready for base preparation.
reports.issue_or_update: The report says the area is ready for base preparation, but does not record a substrate inspection, acceptance, or sign-off.
reports.schedule_status: Base preparation may proceed, subject to confirmation of inspection requirements.
reports.action_required: Confirm whether the substrate inspection has occurred and record acceptance before the pour.
reports.supporting_evidence: No inspection checklist attached

reports.work_planned: Complete base preparation and place replacement concrete if area is released.
reports.work_completed: Base preparation completed over approximately 18 m2. No concrete placed.
reports.issue_or_update: Crew was told verbally at 07:20 that the area was cleared to proceed. No written release or inspection record was available at the workface.
reports.schedule_status: Pour postponed pending written confirmation of substrate acceptance and approved placement details.
reports.action_required: GC/Quality Inspector to issue written release and confirm RFI-017 response status.
reports.responsible_party: General Contractor / Quality Inspector / Design Team
reports.quantity_or_measurement: 18 m2 base preparation; 0 m3 concrete placed
reports.supporting_evidence: Crew foreman notes verbal instruction; no signed inspection form attached

reports.work_planned: Resolve inspection status and coordinate concrete placement.
reports.work_completed: Coordination call held with concrete subcontractor. Superintendent's notes state: 'Inspection passed this morning.'
reports.issue_or_update: No inspector name, inspection time, checklist, or written acceptance is referenced. The subcontractor's report for the same day states that written release was still outstanding at 15:30.
reports.schedule_status: Report indicates inspection passed; subcontractor records indicate pour remains on hold.
reports.action_required: Reconcile inspection status with the inspector and subcontractor; circulate the signed release and confirm whether RFI-017 is answered.
reports.supporting_evidence: Call notes only; no inspection record attached

reports.work_planned: Place replacement concrete after receipt of approved release and mix details.
reports.work_completed: No concrete placed. Crew completed edge cleaning and staged reinforcement materials outside the work area.
reports.materials_equipment: Reinforcement materials staged; concrete pump not mobilized
reports.issue_or_update: At 10:15, foreman checked with the GC. Written inspection release had not been received. RFI-017 asks whether the replacement slab should match the original thickness or revised detail; no response was available to the crew.
reports.schedule_status: Pour postponed for a second shift. Crew reassigned for part of the afternoon.
reports.action_required: Issue inspection release and provide written response to RFI-017 before rescheduling the pour.
reports.responsible_party: General Contractor / Quality Inspector / Design Team
reports.supporting_evidence: Foreman log; no formal response attached

reports.work_planned: Review RFI and confirm repair scope.
reports.work_completed: RFI-017 reviewed internally. Engineer's note says 'use original detail' but the response was not transmitted through the formal RFI system.
reports.issue_or_update: Internal note may be interpreted as a decision, but there is no formally issued response or confirmation that the subcontractor received it.
reports.schedule_status: Subcontractor may remain on hold until formal response is distributed.
reports.action_required: Issue the formal RFI response, confirm receipt, and identify the applicable drawing revision.
reports.supporting_evidence: Internal engineering note; formal response not attached

reports.work_planned: Verify substrate and pre-pour readiness.
reports.work_completed: Inspection completed at 08:10. Substrate accepted for placement subject to using the approved slab detail and documenting reinforcement placement. Signed checklist recorded as QC-B104-0514.
reports.issue_or_update: The signed checklist confirms substrate acceptance, but does not resolve the slab thickness question in RFI-017.
reports.schedule_status: Substrate inspection closed; pour still depends on design clarification and reinforcement verification.
reports.action_required: Design Team to issue formal slab detail; subcontractor to request reinforcement inspection before placement.
reports.supporting_evidence: Signed checklist QC-B104-0514 referenced

ISS-01.note: Quotes the observed water damage and unconfirmed source with needs_verification and no invented cause.

ISS-02.note: Preserves the initial missing formal acceptance/release and closes substrate acceptance using explicit acceptance and signed checklist QC-B104-0514.

ISS-03.note: Preserves apparent readiness without inspection sign-off and missing workface release, followed by signed substrate acceptance. It does not treat apparent readiness as proof of acceptance.

ISS-04.note: F3 retains the unresolved historical slab-detail question and latest missing formal revision/response; F4 separately preserves formal issue/receipt uncertainty and reported RFI resolution. Neither proves technical non-resolution.

ISS-05.note: F8 retains actual original postponements, partial-afternoon crew reassignment, prerequisite-specific holds and later physical placement completion in one scope. No independent acceptance/record/quality closure is inferred.

ISS-06.note: Preserves the GC inspection-passed account versus the missing written release and reconciles substrate acceptance through the later signed checklist.

ISS-07.note: Preserves original thickness versus revised detail, internal and informal instruction, missing drawing/revision, and the latest approved-detail claim without its linked formal response.

ISS-08.note: Preserves the internal response not formally transmitted, unconfirmed receipt, missing revision and latest missing formal response evidence.

ISS-09.note: F5 neutrally asks whether a completed/recorded reinforcement inspection exists, with needs_verification and earlier incomplete versus bare later reference. F10 separately retains the explicit attachment task; no pass inferred.

ISS-10.note: Preserves the superintendent resolved label and explicit outstanding formal-response attachment task/missing-response evidence, with open record-task state.

ISS-11.note: F6 preserves delivered-versus-unmeasured placed volume. No output retains explicitly unfinished strength-test follow-up. Partial counts as missed; this concern was already partial in the saved revision-17 candidate source.

ISS-12.note: F7 preserves reported notice versus unestablished foreman receipt; F11 preserves bounded historical restriction, reassignment/resumption, duration and no-full-shift statement. Count this reference once.

findingNotes.F1: Supported unconfirmed water-damage cause, no invented source.
findingNotes.F2: Supported consolidated substrate-acceptance/written-release history, opposing accounts and later signed closure. No distinct unfinished substrate-record task remains.
findingNotes.F3: Supported consolidated technical detail/revision uncertainty; latest approved-detail claim lacks linked formal revision/response. Historical awaiting-design context is retained.
findingNotes.F4: Supported distinct uncertainty about formal technical response issue and crew receipt, with later reported resolution but absent formal response.
findingNotes.F5: Supported neutral verification question about inspection completion/recording; a bare reference is not treated as physical acceptance.
findingNotes.F6: Supported delivered-versus-unmeasured placed volume; no invented actual quantity, waste or test result.
findingNotes.F7: Supported reported advance notice versus unestablished electrical-foreman receipt.
findingNotes.F8: Supported consolidated historical physical pour hold and later placement completion. The scope question and latest pointer constrain resolved to physical work, while separate acceptance/record findings remain open or uncertain.
findingNotes.F9: Supported explicit open formal-RFI-response attachment task, distinct from formal issue/receipt uncertainty.
findingNotes.F10: Supported explicit open reinforcement-record attachment task, distinct from physical inspection uncertainty.
findingNotes.F11: Supported ended local electrical-trade restriction with bounded duration and reassignment/resumption, distinct from still-unverified notice receipt.

sourceInventory.quote: Set canopy column B-17 after signed bearing-surface acceptance and the issued base layout are available.
Column remained on the lifting frame.
Crew held at B-17 from 08:00 to 10:00, then reassigned to bolt the handrail in the adjacent bay.
The site coordinator verbally advised at 08:10 that the bearing inspection had passed.
The installer had no signed bearing release at 10:00.
The issued anchor-layout revision was also awaited.
The September 1 column-setting window was deferred.
The recorded hold was two hours; no project completion-date effect has been assessed.
Bearing release BR-B17 requested; layout instruction LI-017
Provide the signed bearing release and issued layout before setting B-17.
One column remained unset.
Installer daily log records the 08:00-10:00 hold and reassignment.
Close the written bearing release and issue the approved anchor layout.
Signed bearing release BR-B17-0902 issued at 09:00 and acknowledged by the steel foreperson at 09:15.
Approved anchor layout S-117 revision 7 issued through the document register at 11:00.
BR-B17-0902 explicitly accepts the bearing surface for B-17; it does not cover the later anchor-torque witness.
Revision 7 replaces revision 6.
The register confirms the layout issue to the site coordinator, but no steel-crew receipt acknowledgement is linked.
The bearing-acceptance gate is closed.
Column setting is planned for September 3; physical setting is not reported complete today.
BR-B17-0902; LI-017; S-117 revision 7; transmittal TR-119
Obtain and link the steel foreperson's receipt acknowledgement for S-117 revision 7.
One accepted bearing surface.
Signed bearing release and foreperson acknowledgement filed.
TR-119 records formal layout issue; crew receipt remains unverified.
Set and grout B-17 using S-117 revision 7.
Column B-17 set, aligned and base grouted.
Physical setting and grouting are complete.
Anchor bolts torqued with the calibrated wrench.
The engineer attended the anchor-torque witness.
The daily log cites TW-B17-0903, but the signed witness acceptance sheet is not available in the shared folder.
No test failure is reported.
Physical setting is complete following the earlier two-hour hold.
Automatic acceptance of the separate torque record is not claimed.
S-117 revision 7; TW-B17-0903
Locate the signed torque-witness acceptance sheet and verify its result before closeout.
Six anchor bolts torqued.
Lifting log records completed setting.
Grout placement log filed.
TW-B17-0903 is a reference only; its signed result sheet is unavailable.
Check the closeout folder and continue grout protection.
Delivery count and material certificates checked and accepted.
Column remains protected; no further installation work is outstanding.
BR-B17-0902 remains signed and acknowledged.
The signed TW-B17-0903 result sheet is still unavailable, so anchor-torque acceptance cannot be verified from the register reference alone.
TR-119 remains formally issued, but the steel-crew receipt acknowledgement has not been located.
Grout strength testing is scheduled for September 5 at 10:00 and has not yet occurred.
The planned test is not overdue.
BR-B17-0902; TW-B17-0903; TR-119; grout sample GS-B17
Maintain grout protection until the required strength result is documented.
Obtain the torque-witness result sheet and the steel-crew layout receipt acknowledgement.
Three grout cubes retained for the scheduled test.
Delivery and material checks accepted.
No grout-strength result is available before the scheduled test.

D-01.note: Retains recurring oily film, unknown origin and investigation before return to service without inventing a diagnosis or delay linkage.

D-02.note: Together retain verbal clearance/QC-passed telephone accounts versus absent signed crew release, followed by signed BF-P6-0910 receipt. Resolved applies only to bearing-face release.

D-03.note: Retains 6 mm versus 9 mm conflict, internal draft and later signed TQ-061/M-214 revision D selecting 9 mm, with resolved technical-choice scope.

D-04.note: Retains unissued internal draft and missing installer revision, followed by formal issue at 13:10 and actual chargehand receipt at 13:35; the historical communication gap is closed.

D-05.note: Retains September 9 and 10 actual deferrals, earlier release/revision context and closure of those gates. No output selects September 12 physical setting/grouting completion. Closing individual readiness gates cannot substitute for complete physical history; partial counts missed.

D-06.note: Retains bearing-face-only inspection scope, separate torque witness/acceptance requirement, later AT-P6-0912 reference and inaccessible/unlinked signed sheet. Needs verification does not claim a failed or never-performed inspection.

D-07.note: Retains 22 bags received, 19 issued, 2 returned and 1 unreconciled, with open store-transfer reconciliation and no invented theft or excess volume.

D-08.note: Retains preliminary 0.18 mm versus 0.10 mm limit and final alignment after cure before start-up, with open state rather than failed final acceptance or overdue cure.

D-09.note: Together retain reportedly sent notice, unestablished receipt, 80-minute restriction, three technicians reassigned and restored rack access. Physical restriction and notice receipt remain separately scoped.

findingNotes.F1: Supported unconfirmed cause and source-attributed investigation.
findingNotes.F2: Supported closed written bearing-face release/receipt; F8 preserves the complementary initial verbal/passed context.
findingNotes.F3: Supported technical choice and actual formal issue/receipt closure. Its evidence covers both reference dimensions without claiming an independent second concern.
findingNotes.F4: Supported independent anchor-torque acceptance verification and signed-record linkage. The prerequisite/grouting-dependency candidate is correctly included as context here, with no extra delay card or implication that no inspection occurred.
findingNotes.F5: Supported open one-bag reconciliation.
findingNotes.F6: Supported preliminary alignment discrepancy and remaining final alignment.
findingNotes.F7: Supported uncertain advance-notice receipt, distinct from historical access resumption in F10.
findingNotes.F8: Supported actual historical setting deferrals and closure of the named release/revision gates. Narrow question avoids asserting physical completion, which is missing from selected evidence.
findingNotes.F9: Supported historical instrumentation restriction, three-person reassignment, 80-minute duration and resumed rack access. It remains distinct from uncertain notice receipt in F7.

evaluation.notes: Staged matched D consolidation: two whole-request-hash-verified original revision-18f responses plus two actual new revision-18j repair/scope calls. Nine cards, 8/9 fully found with unchanged partial D-05, zero unsupported distinct findings and zero semantic duplicate cards. All eight exact prior fully found IDs survive. The cross-aspect repair reclassifies the sole invalid candidate as supporting-record context and merges it with the anchor-acceptance record concern, preserving original evidence. The work-progress question narrowly concerns closure of named release/revision gates; it does not claim actual later physical setting/grouting completion, which was absent from saved candidates. New segment 283.575 seconds, n=1, excludes reused inference and is not complete-review latency. Prior rejected and semantic-failed D attempts remain retained; source/reference definitions are unchanged.

ISS-04.note: Supported technical and communication cards retain earlier unanswered RFI, informal/internal direction, later reported resolution and the still-unverified formal response/revision. F4 exact compound source quotes legitimately include RFI status/response; its wrong internal inspection-release component label is not rendered as a product assertion.

ISS-05.note: F8 now contains the actual dated postponements, release/design/reinforcement prerequisites and later physical placement completion in ONE complete work-progress chronology. Resolved is limited to physical placement, not independent acceptance, record or testing requirements.

ISS-06.note: Preserves the GC inspection-passed account versus the missing written release and reconciles substrate acceptance through the later signed checklist.

ISS-07.note: Preserves original thickness versus revised detail, internal and informal instruction, missing drawing/revision, and the latest approved-detail claim without its linked formal response.

ISS-08.note: Supported cards retain internal/informal instruction, unconfirmed formal transmission/receipt, unidentified revision and latest missing response record. Internal component-label errors are recorded separately from rendered factual support.

ISS-09.note: Supported work chronology retains the requested-but-not-completed reinforcement prerequisite and later bare inspection reference; the separate needs-verification record card requires the missing inspection record. No supported card treats physical completion or a bare ID as proven inspection acceptance. Unsupported F5 is excluded from reference credit.

ISS-10.note: F4 retains reported RFI resolution versus unverified formal issue/receipt; F9 independently retains the formal-response attachment gap. No completed formal response is inferred.

ISS-11.note: F6 retains delivered versus unmeasured placed quantity. F11 explicitly selects the latest source stating curing/protection and strength-test follow-up remain in progress, with open quality-follow-up state. Source-only reconsideration restored this task after an incorrect initial routine verdict; full trace retained.

ISS-12.note: F7 retains reported notice versus unestablished advance foreman receipt. F12 retains bounded historical restriction and reassignment/resumption. Count once; no full-shift or critical-path claim.

findingNotes.F1: Supported unconfirmed cause, no invented source.
findingNotes.F2: Supported substrate-only acceptance/release chronology and signed closure; written-record discrepancy is consolidated into that acceptance gate.
findingNotes.F3: Supported approved slab-detail/revision uncertainty; does not prove technical non-resolution after reported RFI closure.
findingNotes.F4: Supported final card: its exact compound source quotations contain the RFI status/response clauses that match its question. The internal ledger wrongly labels the closed substrate inspection-release component as represented here, but that component label is not rendered; the full S051 quote was already present before the audit. This internal classification defect is not counted as a new unsupported product assertion.
findingNotes.F5: Unsupported under the whole-finding subject-association rule: newly attached S037/S039 concern the earlier substrate inspection-passed versus missing-release discrepancy, closed separately by signed substrate acceptance. This card asks about reinforcement inspection and now presents those substrate passages as represented requirements for reinforcement. Generic inspection wording does not establish the same physical subject. Original valid reinforcement evidence remains, but cannot cure the added material conflation.
findingNotes.F6: Supported delivered-versus-unmeasured placed quantity, no invented actual volume or waste.
findingNotes.F7: Supported final card: reported electrical notification and uncertain advance receipt remain correctly scoped. The ledger internally maps safe-access release notification to advance receipt, a different temporal obligation. The component label is not rendered and S093 was already source context before the audit; record this internal defect without treating it as a newly invented product claim.
findingNotes.F8: Supported complete physical pour-hold chronology through completion. All prerequisite-specific fragments now consolidated; no separate residual hold card.
findingNotes.F9: Supported formal-RFI-response document attachment/availability gap, independent of technical issue/receipt and the separately required reinforcement record.
findingNotes.F10: Supported reinforcement-record attachment/availability requirement, independent of whether physical acceptance can be established. No RFI-only scope hides this task.
findingNotes.F11: Supported explicit remaining curing/protection and strength-test follow-up, open; no failed, overdue or completed test inferred.
findingNotes.F12: Supported ended bounded electrical-trade restriction and reassignment/resumption, independent of notice receipt.

sourceInventory.quote: Set canopy column B-17 after signed bearing-surface acceptance and the issued base layout are available.
Column remained on the lifting frame.
Crew held at B-17 from 08:00 to 10:00, then reassigned to bolt the handrail in the adjacent bay.
The site coordinator verbally advised at 08:10 that the bearing inspection had passed.
The installer had no signed bearing release at 10:00.
The issued anchor-layout revision was also awaited.
The September 1 column-setting window was deferred.
The recorded hold was two hours; no project completion-date effect has been assessed.
Bearing release BR-B17 requested; layout instruction LI-017
Provide the signed bearing release and issued layout before setting B-17.
One column remained unset.
Installer daily log records the 08:00-10:00 hold and reassignment.
Close the written bearing release and issue the approved anchor layout.
Signed bearing release BR-B17-0902 issued at 09:00 and acknowledged by the steel foreperson at 09:15.
Approved anchor layout S-117 revision 7 issued through the document register at 11:00.
BR-B17-0902 explicitly accepts the bearing surface for B-17; it does not cover the later anchor-torque witness.
Revision 7 replaces revision 6.
The register confirms the layout issue to the site coordinator, but no steel-crew receipt acknowledgement is linked.
The bearing-acceptance gate is closed.
Column setting is planned for September 3; physical setting is not reported complete today.
BR-B17-0902; LI-017; S-117 revision 7; transmittal TR-119
Obtain and link the steel foreperson's receipt acknowledgement for S-117 revision 7.
One accepted bearing surface.
Signed bearing release and foreperson acknowledgement filed.
TR-119 records formal layout issue; crew receipt remains unverified.
Set and grout B-17 using S-117 revision 7.
Column B-17 set, aligned and base grouted.
Physical setting and grouting are complete.
Anchor bolts torqued with the calibrated wrench.
The engineer attended the anchor-torque witness.
The daily log cites TW-B17-0903, but the signed witness acceptance sheet is not available in the shared folder.
No test failure is reported.
Physical setting is complete following the earlier two-hour hold.
Automatic acceptance of the separate torque record is not claimed.
S-117 revision 7; TW-B17-0903
Locate the signed torque-witness acceptance sheet and verify its result before closeout.
Six anchor bolts torqued.
Lifting log records completed setting.
Grout placement log filed.
TW-B17-0903 is a reference only; its signed result sheet is unavailable.
Check the closeout folder and continue grout protection.
Delivery count and material certificates checked and accepted.
Column remains protected; no further installation work is outstanding.
BR-B17-0902 remains signed and acknowledged.
The signed TW-B17-0903 result sheet is still unavailable, so anchor-torque acceptance cannot be verified from the register reference alone.
TR-119 remains formally issued, but the steel-crew receipt acknowledgement has not been located.
Grout strength testing is scheduled for September 5 at 10:00 and has not yet occurred.
The planned test is not overdue.
BR-B17-0902; TW-B17-0903; TR-119; grout sample GS-B17
Maintain grout protection until the required strength result is documented.
Obtain the torque-witness result sheet and the steel-crew layout receipt acknowledgement.
Three grout cubes retained for the scheduled test.
Delivery and material checks accepted.
No grout-strength result is available before the scheduled test.

G-01.note: Retains the verbal passed-bearing account versus absent signed release, then dated signed issue and foreperson acknowledgement; resolved applies to bearing release only.

G-02.note: Explicitly retains unavailable signed torque-witness result and the latest source statement that separate anchor-torque acceptance cannot be verified from the register ID alone. No failed or never-performed test is inferred; bearing release is independently closed in F1. The attended-witness detail is not quoted, a contextual omission, but the material acceptance/record distinction and latest uncertainty are preserved.

G-03.note: Retains September 1 08:00-10:00 hold, handrail reassignment, missing release/layout context, two-hour duration and September 3 physical setting/grouting completion in one chronology. Resolved is physical completion only; no project completion-date effect is inferred.

G-04.note: Retains scheduled September 5 at 10:00 strength testing, not-yet-performed status, unavailable result and the explicit requirement to maintain grout protection until the strength result is documented. Both parts of the unchanged compound reference are visible under the open quality concern; no overdue/failure or premature release is inferred.

G-05.note: Retains formally issued layout/TR-119 versus missing linked steel-crew receipt acknowledgement and the still-open acknowledgement task after physical installation. It does not claim no formal instruction was issued.

findingNotes.F4: Supported complete historical setting hold through later physical completion, distinct from open closeout/testing/receipt.
findingNotes.F5: Supported scheduled but unperformed strength testing plus the explicit ongoing protection-until-documented-result condition. The requirement is visible in both exact source passages and coverageRequirements; no second redundant card is added.

D-01.note: Retains recurring oily film, unknown origin and investigation before return to service without inventing a diagnosis or delay linkage.

D-02.note: Together retain verbal clearance/QC-passed telephone accounts versus absent signed crew release, followed by signed BF-P6-0910 receipt. Resolved applies only to bearing-face release.

D-03.note: Retains 6 mm versus 9 mm conflict, internal draft and later signed TQ-061/M-214 revision D selecting 9 mm, with resolved technical-choice scope.

D-04.note: Retains unissued internal draft and missing installer revision, followed by formal issue at 13:10 and actual chargehand receipt at 13:35; the historical communication gap is closed.

D-05.note: Retains September 9 and 10 actual deferrals, earlier release/revision context and closure of those gates. No output selects September 12 physical setting/grouting completion. Closing individual readiness gates cannot substitute for complete physical history; partial counts missed.

D-06.note: Retains bearing-face-only inspection scope, separate torque witness/acceptance requirement, later AT-P6-0912 reference and inaccessible/unlinked signed sheet. Needs verification does not claim a failed or never-performed inspection.

D-07.note: Retains 22 bags received, 19 issued, 2 returned and 1 unreconciled, with open store-transfer reconciliation and no invented theft or excess volume.

D-08.note: Retains preliminary 0.18 mm versus 0.10 mm limit and final alignment after cure before start-up, with open state rather than failed final acceptance or overdue cure.

D-09.note: Together retain reportedly sent notice, unestablished receipt, 80-minute restriction, three technicians reassigned and restored rack access. Physical restriction and notice receipt remain separately scoped.

findingNotes.F1: Supported unconfirmed cause and source-attributed investigation.
findingNotes.F2: Supported closed written bearing-face release/receipt; F8 preserves the complementary initial verbal/passed context.
findingNotes.F3: Supported technical choice and actual formal issue/receipt closure. Its evidence covers both reference dimensions without claiming an independent second concern.
findingNotes.F4: Supported independent anchor-torque acceptance verification and signed-record linkage. The prerequisite/grouting-dependency candidate is correctly included as context here, with no extra delay card or implication that no inspection occurred.
findingNotes.F5: Supported open one-bag reconciliation.
findingNotes.F6: Supported preliminary alignment discrepancy and remaining final alignment.
findingNotes.F7: Supported uncertain advance-notice receipt, distinct from historical access resumption in F10.
findingNotes.F8: Supported actual historical setting deferrals and closure of the named release/revision gates. Narrow question avoids asserting physical completion, which is missing from selected evidence.
findingNotes.F9: Supported historical instrumentation restriction, three-person reassignment, 80-minute duration and resumed rack access. It remains distinct from uncertain notice receipt in F7.

ISS-01.note: Quotes the observed water damage and unconfirmed source with needs_verification and no invented cause.

ISS-02.note: Preserves the initial missing formal acceptance/release and closes substrate acceptance using explicit acceptance and signed checklist QC-B104-0514.

ISS-03.note: Preserves apparent readiness without inspection sign-off and missing workface release, followed by signed substrate acceptance. It does not treat apparent readiness as proof of acceptance.

ISS-04.note: Supported technical and communication cards retain earlier unanswered RFI, informal/internal direction, later reported resolution and the still-unverified formal response/revision. F4 exact compound source quotes legitimately include RFI status/response; its wrong internal inspection-release component label is not rendered as a product assertion.

ISS-05.note: F8 now contains the actual dated postponements, release/design/reinforcement prerequisites and later physical placement completion in ONE complete work-progress chronology. Resolved is limited to physical placement, not independent acceptance, record or testing requirements.

ISS-06.note: Preserves the GC inspection-passed account versus the missing written release and reconciles substrate acceptance through the later signed checklist.

ISS-07.note: Preserves original thickness versus revised detail, internal and informal instruction, missing drawing/revision, and the latest approved-detail claim without its linked formal response.

ISS-08.note: Supported cards retain internal/informal instruction, unconfirmed formal transmission/receipt, unidentified revision and latest missing response record. Internal component-label errors are recorded separately from rendered factual support.

ISS-09.note: Supported work chronology retains the requested-but-not-completed reinforcement prerequisite and later bare inspection reference; the separate needs-verification record card requires the missing inspection record. No supported card treats physical completion or a bare ID as proven inspection acceptance. Unsupported F5 is excluded from reference credit.

ISS-10.note: F4 retains reported RFI resolution versus unverified formal issue/receipt; F9 independently retains the formal-response attachment gap. No completed formal response is inferred.

ISS-11.note: F6 retains delivered versus unmeasured placed quantity. F11 explicitly selects the latest source stating curing/protection and strength-test follow-up remain in progress, with open quality-follow-up state. Source-only reconsideration restored this task after an incorrect initial routine verdict; full trace retained.

ISS-12.note: F7 retains reported notice versus unestablished advance foreman receipt. F12 retains bounded historical restriction and reassignment/resumption. Count once; no full-shift or critical-path claim.

findingNotes.F1: Supported unconfirmed cause, no invented source.
findingNotes.F2: Supported substrate-only acceptance/release chronology and signed closure; written-record discrepancy is consolidated into that acceptance gate.
findingNotes.F3: Supported approved slab-detail/revision uncertainty; does not prove technical non-resolution after reported RFI closure.
findingNotes.F4: Supported final card: its exact compound source quotations contain the RFI status/response clauses that match its question. The internal ledger wrongly labels the closed substrate inspection-release component as represented here, but that component label is not rendered; the full S051 quote was already present before the audit. This internal classification defect is not counted as a new unsupported product assertion.
findingNotes.F5: Unsupported wrong-subject augmentation remains: S039 from May12 has generic inspection reconciliation and signed release, with no reinforcement subject in that report. The gate newly attaches it to the narrow reinforcement question despite the separate earlier acceptance chronology. Source ambiguity cannot establish reinforcement acceptance context. Valid original reinforcement evidence does not cure this new material subject association.
findingNotes.F6: Supported delivered-versus-unmeasured placed quantity, no invented actual volume or waste.
findingNotes.F7: Supported final card: reported electrical notification and uncertain advance receipt remain correctly scoped. The ledger internally maps safe-access release notification to advance receipt, a different temporal obligation. The component label is not rendered and S093 was already source context before the audit; record this internal defect without treating it as a newly invented product claim.
findingNotes.F8: Supported complete physical pour-hold chronology through completion. All prerequisite-specific fragments now consolidated; no separate residual hold card.
findingNotes.F9: Supported formal-RFI-response document attachment/availability gap, independent of technical issue/receipt and the separately required reinforcement record.
findingNotes.F10: Supported reinforcement-record attachment/availability requirement, independent of whether physical acceptance can be established. No RFI-only scope hides this task.
findingNotes.F11: Supported explicit remaining curing/protection and strength-test follow-up, open; no failed, overdue or completed test inferred.
findingNotes.F12: Supported ended bounded electrical-trade restriction and reassignment/resumption, independent of notice receipt.
findingNotes.F13: Unsupported latest-state interpretation: the new needs-verification pour-conflict card cites only historical S037 and omits the later signed acceptance and physical placement already retained in F2/F8. It reopens the earlier pass-versus-hold conflict as a current unknown without source evidence of a separate remaining reconciliation task. This also repeats existing history, but is counted unsupported under the whole-finding rule rather than receiving duplicate-only treatment.
findingNotes.F14: Supported independent drawing-revision identification/citation task. The technical slab-thickness question, formal RFI communication and attached response are separately answerable from identifying the actual approved drawing revision. Source S060/S081 explicitly requires that identification; no drawing number, issue time or completed state is invented. Overlapping context alone does not make this card duplicate.

evaluation.notes: Accepted machine output but FAILED final-output semantic gate. Fourteen cards retain12/12 reference concerns across supported alternatives, with two unsupported whole findings: F5 wrong-subject S039 augmentation and F13 stale reopened historical conflict. Zero duplicate-only cards; F13 also repeats previously covered history but material wrong state takes precedence. New F14 drawing-revision identification is a legitimate independent task, so card count14 alone is not a failure. All24prior candidate indices and three new atomic additions survive once, preserving all selected evidence. Twenty-seven whole-request-hash-verified earlier responses plus ten actual new calls (seven source-isolated attachment reviews and three consolidation calls);731.019-second new segment is not continuous full-review latency. Original source/reference definitions are unchanged; no clean-release claim.
